To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the Kolb Inventory of Learning Styles (ILS) and Felder Silverman Learning Styles Index (LSI) have adequate levels of validity; 2. the reliability levels of all scales are below the acceptable levels; 3.

the four sub-scales of Kolb's Inventory of Learning Styles and the four sub-scales of Felder-Silverman's Index of Learning Style Questionnaire have adequate validity, but their internal consistency is low.

(1) the four sub scales of the Kolb inventory and the four sub scales from the Felder Silverman questionnaire have acceptable validity indexes; (2) however, the reliability indexes obtained with Cronbach’s alpha are under the acceptable levels in all sub scales; and (3) we suggest more studies with diverse university samples to confirm the psychometric properties of these instruments in this type of population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the psychometric properties of two instruments that measure learning styles, Kolb's Learning Style Inventory (LSI) and Felder and Silverman's Index of Learning Styles (ILS).
the development and validation of a questionnaire for the assessment of the learning styles of the Chilean students.
the study of the psychometric properties of Kolb's Learning Styles Inventory (LSI) and Felder-Silverman's Learning Style Index (LSI) in a sample of Physical Education students of Chile.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Kolb's Inventory of Learning Styles and the Felder and Silverman's Index of Learning Styles are not valid and reliable instruments for assessing the learning styles of physical education students in Chile.
the results of the current study suggest that the Felder Silverman Index of Learning Styles and the Learning Style Inventory are not appropriate for use with Chilean Physical Education students.
the results of this study suggest the need to continue with the research on the psychometric properties of the instruments used in order to improve their validity and reliability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Kolb Inventory of Learning Style and the Felder-Silverman Learning Style Index show acceptable levels of validity, but not of reliability.
the two inventories have adequate indices of validity, but the indices of reliability obtained with Cronbach's alpha are below acceptable levels for all sub-scales.
the Kolb Learning Style Inventory and the Felder-Silverman Learning Style Index are useful instruments in the study of learning styles in physical education students.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single instrument for assessing learning styles in higher education is not advisable.

the use of a combination of Kolb’s Inventory of Learning Styles (ILS) and Felder and Silverman’s Index of Learning Styles (ISL) can be used to help identify the preferred styles of learning for students.
the two instruments have good validity, but low reliability.
